proposition_chain.statement: Disclosure theory holds that an informed manager may rationally withhold private information when disclosure is costly, and that non-disclosure can persist in equilibrium because outside investors cannot distinguish a manager who is uninformed from one who is informed but silent, so a withholding state is itself informative.
proposition_chain.reason: M1 context (cont.): installs the disclosure-state lens, the theoretical foundation that a withholding state is meaningful. Theory is the LENS (voluntary withholding); the legal cites in IN.3 establish THIS firm is in such a state (do not conflate).

proposition_chain.statement: A firm privately committed to an acquisition it has not announced sits in a concrete such state: preliminary merger negotiations can be material before any definitive agreement, and although the firm may stay silent it may not mislead once it speaks, so the executive can neither confirm nor deny the pending deal and is left to answer around it.
proposition_chain.reason: M1 core phenomenon (the disclosure bind), the paper's organizing primitive, grounded in the legal setting. Materiality scoped to the acquirer (Basic = 'can be material', not 'every deal is MNPI'); no legal-gag overclaim.

proposition_chain.statement: The purpose of this study is to ask whether CEO question-and-answer uncertainty tracks a deal's passage from private to public: whether it is elevated while an acquisition is withheld and recedes once it is announced. We construct a residual measure of CEO question-and-answer uncertainty (UncResCEO) that nets out each CEO's persistent speaking style, following the decomposition of the call-language literature, and defer its construction and the estimating equations to Section 2.
proposition_chain.reason: M2 objective + method: the explicit pivot ('The purpose of this study is to...'), states the research question (the mirror target for the conclusion's M1), and NAMES the measure pointing to Section 2 (boundary: names, does not re-derive). DWZ may be named here as the measure's origin (allowed in the intro, unlike the abstract).
